pathways.name: Uptake → processing → bile
pathways.summary: Blood contents cross the fenestrated endothelium into the space of Disse and are taken up by microvilli on the sinusoidal face; they are processed in the endoplasmic reticulum, handled by the Golgi and vesicular traffic, and secreted across the canalicular membrane into bile, which flows counter-current to blood.
transportersEnzymes: NTCP (SLC10A1) and OATP1B1/1B3 at the sinusoidal face
CYP450 and UGT1A1 in the smooth ER
BSEP (ABCB11), MRP2 (ABCC2), ABCG5/G8 at the canalicular membrane
pathways.compartmentRoute: Sinusoid → LSEC fenestra → space of Disse → sinusoidal microvilli → cytosol → smooth ER → Golgi / vesicles → canalicular membrane → bile canaliculus → toward the bile ductule
pathways.direction: Blood flows one way along the sinusoid; bile flows the opposite way along the canaliculus (toward the portal tract).
pathways.clinical: Cholestasis when any step fails: sinusoidal uptake (NTCP/OATP), ER conjugation (e.g. UGT1A1 in Gilbert and Crigler–Najjar), or canalicular export (BSEP in PFIC2 and drug-induced cholestasis; MRP2 in Dubin–Johnson).
